source: NCERT Class VI, Exploring Society: India and Beyond, Geography Ch. 3.

sections.heading: 1. Landforms — The Shape of the Land
points: **Landforms** are the natural features of the Earth's surface: **mountains, plateaus and plains**.
They are shaped over long periods by **internal forces** (movements inside the Earth) and **external forces** (weathering and **erosion** by rivers, wind, glaciers, waves).
The wearing away of land is **erosion**; the laying down of material is **deposition**.

sections.heading: 2. Mountains
points: **Mountains** are high, steep landforms; the highest peak is **Mount Everest** (Himalayas).

sub: **Fold mountains** — formed by folding of the crust (e.g. **Himalayas**, the world's highest, and young).
**Block mountains** — formed when land between faults is raised or the sides sink.

points: Mountains are sources of **rivers**, store **snow/ice**, have rich **biodiversity**, but life there is **hard** (cold, steep, thin population).

sections.heading: 3. Plateaus
points: A **plateau** is an elevated flat-topped highland ("tableland"), higher than the plains around it.
The **Deccan Plateau** is one of the oldest and most stable; the **Chota Nagpur Plateau** is rich in **minerals**.
The **East African Plateau** and the **Tibetan Plateau** (the highest, 'Roof of the World') are examples.
Plateaus are storehouses of **minerals**; they also have **waterfalls** where rivers plunge to the plains.

sections.heading: 4. Plains
points: **Plains** are large stretches of **flat, low land**, often very **fertile**.
Most are formed by **rivers depositing silt (alluvium)** — e.g. the **Indo-Gangetic plains**.
Plains are the most **densely populated** and **agriculturally productive** regions; easy for **farming, settlement and transport**.

sections.heading: 5. Landforms and Human Life
points: Each landform offers different opportunities: plains → farming and dense settlement; mountains → tourism, forests, rivers; plateaus → mining.
People **adapt** their houses, clothing and livelihoods to the landform and climate.
Landforms must be used **responsibly** — over-use causes soil erosion, landslides and loss of forests.

sections.heading: 6. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Three major landforms: mountains, plateaus, plains.
Himalayas = fold mountains (highest, young); Everest = highest peak.
Mountain types: fold, block, volcanic.
Deccan = old stable plateau; Chota Nagpur = mineral-rich; Tibet = highest plateau.
Plains = flat, fertile, formed by river silt (alluvium); most densely populated.
Erosion = wearing away; deposition = laying down.

sections.heading: 7. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **Himalayas are fold mountains** and geologically **young**.
A **plateau** is a raised **flat-topped** highland — not a mountain or a plain.
Plains are usually formed by **deposition** of river silt, making them fertile.
**Chota Nagpur Plateau** is the mineral-rich one in India.
